title: Proctor Quality and Learning Manager, Scaling Operations
description:
Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. It’s a big mission, and that’s where you come in!

At Duolingo, you’ll join a team that cares about educating our users, experimenting with big ideas, making fact-based decisions, and finding innovative solutions to complex problems. You’ll have limitless learning opportunities and daily collaborations with world-class minds — while doing work that’s both meaningful and fun.

Join our life-changing mission to develop education for our half a billion (and growing!) learners around the world. 

Read our blog to learn more.

About the role...

The Duolingo English Test (DET) is a high-stakes assessment used by institutions around the world. Its integrity depends on proctors making accurate, consistent, and defensible decisions — even when sessions present ambiguous evidence or new forms of cheating. As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program.

🧠  You will...

  • Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases.
  • Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable.
  • Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes.
  • Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance.
  • Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly.
  • Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable.
  • Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering.
  • Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality.
  • Connect human and technology-assisted quality — establish benchmarks for AI-assisted workflows and validate automated capabilities against real sessions before deployment.

✅  You have...

  • 5+ years in assessment development, scoring/rater quality, certification, quality assurance, or a field involving complex, consequential judgments; experience aligning reviewers to a shared standard through calibration programs.
  • Adult-learning program experience spanning onboarding, certification, ongoing training, remediation, and effectiveness measurement (beyond one-off materials).
  • Exceptional attention to detail and strong judgment in ambiguous cases; ability to produce clear, defensible decisions and guidance.
  • Analytical fluency to interpret quality data, disagreement patterns, and performance trends and translate them into practical interventions.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; ability to turn complex standards into precise, usable guidance and explain difficult calls.
  • Cross-functional leadership without formal authority; experience directing contractors or partners toward clear accountability and outcomes.
  • Demonstrated skill in quality standards and rubric design, building living systems with decision logs, change histories, and controls for auditability.
  • Experience defining quality benchmarks and validation methods for human–technology workflows, including AI-assisted processes.
  • Adaptability — comfort revising standards and programs as risks, products, and technology change.

⭐  Exceptional candidates will have...

  • Experience in language assessment, test security, remote proctoring, trust and safety, or fraud prevention in high-integrity environments.
  • Experience maintaining quality across large, distributed examiner/rater/reviewer/contractor populations.
  • Familiarity with assessment concepts such as inter-rater agreement, reliability, standardization, and performance monitoring.
  • Experience designing quality systems that span human judgment and technology-assisted workflows.
  • Familiarity with learning-management systems, assessment platforms, quality-audit tools, or operational analytics.

title: Tech Lead and Manager (TLM), Production Engineering
description: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About Production Engineering Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. Our Teams Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across four areas: Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs What You'll Do Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure . You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team. As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach : you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes. Day to day, you will: Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership. Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered. Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale. Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved. Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time. Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs. Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers. Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE. Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom. Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done. What We Look For We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team. The mindset we're looking for: You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems. You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen. You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less. We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp. This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better. You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it. This role is for you if you’re excited by: Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same. Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality. Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional. The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary. What You'll Do Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers. Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver. Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path. Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room. Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use. Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down. Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools. Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards. Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system. Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it. What You Need Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes. Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple. Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped. Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications. Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it. Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale. Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. You connect system decisions to real workflows and customer outcomes. The ability to create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and maintain momentum without losing the quality bar. Curiosity that borders on obsession about how AI changes software and how we build it—and the ability to ignite that curiosity in others. Nice to Haves Experience building agent-usable design guidance, generation workflows, or evaluations for design quality. Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams’ daily workflow. Experience leading a major design-system migration or company-wide change in how teams build. Experience evolving a system across platforms or connecting product and brand experiences. Founder or early-stage startup experience. About Production Engineering Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. Our Teams Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across four areas: Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs What You'll Do Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure . Day to day, you will: Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale. Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved. Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time. Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers. Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE. Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom. Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. As a member of Ramp's Risk Strategy & Operations team, you will leverage data to develop and optimize credit strategies. Credit is one of Ramp's most consequential products. Every policy change affects how customers can grow their usage, and how responsibly Ramp scales up while managing risk. Credit Risk Strategy owns these tradeoffs end to end. In this role, you will own or help build strategy across credit risk areas like credit limits, payment speed, and collections. You'll take ambiguous problems, get to the data, prototype the solution, and push the change with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Risk Operations, Finance, Customer Experience, and Compliance. AI fluency is required. We use AI as a core pillar of our risk management stack, and you will be prototyping and managing related Agents and tools. You should already be using tools like Claude Code, Codex, or similar AI tools to write code, explore data, prototype apps, automate workflows, and check your own work. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to use AI to ship something runnable or inspectable enough to test, improve, and hand off. We are looking for builders with high agency and high urgency: people who prototype the workflow, not just write the recommendation for someone else to build. What You'll Do Own credit risk strategy for areas like model prototyping, credit limits, payment speed, collections, etc. Use SQL, quantitative reasoning, and credit risk judgment to investigate patterns, size opportunities, define policy changes, and pressure-test recommendations. Build the first useful version when the workflow does not exist: a tool, app, dashboard, agent, notebook, QA loop, monitor, or decisioning process. Use AI tools every day to move faster on research, analysis, coding, synthesis, writing, verification, and follow-through. This is a backend-leaning role with work spanning the stack. You might build the systems that provision and manage a fleet of customer Postgres instances, design how user-defined schemas evolve safely, or make complex queries execute efficiently. You’ll also follow those systems into the product: improving how a table loads, how users understand a slow operation, or how an agent safely works with their data. You’ll help shape the architecture and the product together. Some problems call for a better abstraction, others for a better default, and others for rethinking what we ask the user to do in the first place. You’ll work with teammates and customers to find those answers, ship practical solutions, and evolve them as usage grows. Our stack includes Postgres, Go, TypeScript, Node.js, and React. About the Team: The people who understand a business best aren’t always the people who can build its software. A support lead knows how tickets should be triaged. An operations manager knows how inventory should move. But turning that knowledge into a reliable system often means finding an engineer, provisioning a database, and building an application. We’re building database infrastructure for everyone else. We want everyday knowledge workers to bring their data into Notion, connect it, and build workflows around it. And do so with the power of a real database (Postgres!) and the approachability of a tool they already know. AI agents make that opportunity even bigger: helping people build and operate systems they couldn’t have created on their own. For our team, this is much more than putting a friendly interface on Postgres. It means making hard database problems disappear from the user’s workflow without sacrificing correctness, performance, or flexibility. How do you let someone reshape a live database as easily as editing a document? Make the right indexes exist without asking someone to become a DBA? Let a weekend experiment grow into a company’s system of record without anyone having to rearchitect it? What You'll Achieve: Take a new product from alpha to general availability. Work with early customers to understand what matters, iterate on feedback, and help shape what we ship. Make real customer workloads fast. Improve query execution, indexing, and client data loading so performance holds up as datasets grow and workflows become more demanding. Build systems businesses can trust with their data. Make schema changes, concurrent writes, permissions, and recovery reliable enough for customers to build essential workflows on top. Make powerful capabilities approachable. Turn database provisioning, migrations, and indexes into a reliable, easy-to-use product experience that gives people the power of a database without the burden of managing one. Build for the customers who come next. Automate database provisioning and fleet operations, strengthen observability, and evolve the architecture so we can serve many, many customers. Skills You'll Need to Bring: Production relational database experience (e.g., Postgres or MySQL). You’ve made decisions about schemas and indexes, analyzed database performance, and debugged issues involving transactions, locking, or concurrency. Your experience goes beyond accessing a database through an ORM. Engineering experience and technical leadership. You bring 10+ years of experience building and operating production software, with a track record of setting technical direction and leading complex, cross-team initiatives from concept through delivery. You identify the most important problems to solve, turn ambiguous goals into a technical strategy, and align engineers and partner teams around a practical plan. You stay hands-on while helping others make better decisions through design reviews, mentorship, and clear technical guidance. Strong backend engineering fundamentals. You’ve built services that need to remain correct under concurrency and failure. You can reason about retries, partial failures, consistency, and the trade-offs involved in reliable reads and writes. A systematic approach to performance. You use query plans, traces, profiles, and experiments to find bottlenecks and verify improvements. You’re willing to follow a problem across storage, services, and client code rather than stopping at a team boundary. Product judgment. You’re interested in who will use what you build, not just how it works. You can turn a customer’s problem into a technical approach and recognize when a better default or simpler workflow would solve it more effectively. Willingness to work across the stack. You bring backend depth, but you’re comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and working in client code when that’s what delivering a good experience requires. Fluency with AI-assisted engineering. You use AI to accelerate exploration, implementation, and testing while taking responsibility for understanding and validating the result. Nice to Haves: Experience managing fleets of databases or building database platforms, including provisioning, upgrades, backups, and recovery. Deep Postgres expertise, such as advanced query optimization, performance tuning, or workload isolation for large datasets and high-concurrency workloads. Experience building query layers, sync engines, change-data-capture pipelines, permission systems, or other reusable data abstractions. You will help deliver complex, production-grade data migrations, integrations, and automations for customers across APAC. This is initially an internally focused, hands-on engineering role. You will partner closely with regional Forward Deployed Engineers, who own customer discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder communication, risk management, and final customer validation. You will create migration infrastructure, standards, and reusable tooling used by FDEs across APAC, while establishing practices that can scale globally. The role offers an opportunity to become a technical authority for production migration delivery, shaping how Notion approaches reliability, validation, and operational quality across complex customer environments. As the team grows, the role may also expand toward customer-facing FDE work, technical leadership, or a deeper engineering path, depending on business needs and demonstrated capability. What You'll Achieve: Own the technical execution layer after customer requirements, scope, and solution architecture have been established with the regional FDE. Contribute to feasibility assessment, estimation, implementation planning, and risk identification while the regional FDE remains accountable for customer discovery, scope, architecture, stakeholder communication, and final acceptance. Apply a repeatable migration lifecycle covering source inventory and sampling, scope and pruning decisions, compatibility and degradation assessment, transformation design, pilot or dry run, user acceptance testing, production cutover, reconciliation, remediation, hypercare, and documented handoff. Translate approved customer and regional FDE requirements into clear technical designs, implementation plans, test strategies, runbooks, and delivery estimates. Build production-quality migration utilities, backend services, data pipelines, integrations, and automations using Python, SQL, APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure. Investigate source-system behavior, data quality issues, permissions, rate limits, authentication constraints, and edge cases, then recommend practical solutions. Design and validate permissions, ownership, and inheritance mappings against the approved migration plan. Make unsupported or ambiguous access requirements explicit, obtain the required decision or approval, and preserve evidence of validation. title: Business Systems Analyst
location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY • United States
description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

As a member of the Operations & Strategy team within Customer Operations & Support (COS), you'll own and evolve the systems that power our support organization. This role is ideal for a well-rounded systems admin with deep Zendesk expertise and experience with Decagon, who enjoys working across many tools and can jump in wherever the team needs support. You'll help keep our support systems stable, well-designed, and adaptable, while partnering across teams to implement changes that improve both customer and Specialist experience.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States. 

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Own and optimize the COS Zendesk environment, including workflows, business rules, automations, routing, permissions, and overall system health
  • Lead improvements to ticket classification, queue design, backlog management, and skills-based routing to help Support scale
  • Administer Decagon and its integration with Zendesk, including handoffs, escalations, and routing of AI-escalated tickets
  • Serve as a hands-on admin across our broader support tooling, including Sprinklr, Gainsight, MaestroQA, Assembled, among others
  • Evaluate and expand agent-facing AI capabilities, including Zendesk Copilot and other agent assist opportunities
  • Own the lifecycle of systems changes, including requirements, design, testing, rollout, communication, and post-launch monitoring
  • Create and maintain documentation across systems, including playbooks, operating procedures, change logs, and architecture diagrams

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 3+ years of experience as a Zendesk administrator or Business Systems Analyst supporting a customer or product support organization
  • Deep hands-on experience with Zendesk workflows, routing, automations, business rules, queue architecture, and channel configuration, plus hands-on experience configuring Decagon and integrating it with Zendesk
  • Experience administering or supporting multiple tools across a support ecosystem, and the ability to learn new systems quickly
  • Experience leading systems changes independently or in partnership with Engineering, IT, Security, or Analytics
  • Strong communication skills, ownership, and sound judgment, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders while maintaining a high bar for quality, documentation, and execution

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Zendesk Administrator certification
  • Experience configuring skills-based routing, intelligent routing, or classification
  • Experience with Zendesk Copilot, agent assist, or other AI-powered support tooling
  • Admin experience with Sprinklr, Gainsight, MaestroQA, Assembled, or Salesforce
  • Experience with APIs, webhooks, custom Zendesk apps, or scripting, plus SQL or analytics tools to evaluate workflow and tooling performance

title: Copy of Manager I, Engineering - Language Platform
description:
Application Performance Monitoring (APM) is one of Datadog’s premier products that helps developers see inside complex distributed systems. Our SDKs are both the delivery vehicle for APM and the platform on which all of Datadog’s service and app based products (e.g. Application Security Management, Profiling, Data Stream Monitoring…) are delivered. We believe our SDKs are one of our technical moats and are a key competitive advantage for APM and Datadog more broadly. They’re also open-source.

Leading the evolution of our SDKs is a technically demanding and highly collaborative effort. You’ll work with language experts to deliver cutting-edge observability products across our 9 supported languages, with industry leading performance and a world class developer experience. You’ll rethink our SDKs’ architecture, APIs, data models, and protocol to meet Datadog’s current needs and scale, all while building in the open. And you’ll grow your team’s capacity by fostering a culture focused on customer needs, continuous learning, and innovation. 

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager who cares as much about technical excellence as empowering other engineering teams. 

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, grow, and develop a team of roughly 4-8 library engineers — coaching, giving direct feedback, and empowering senior ICs as technical leaders owning outcomes
  • Own team delivery and productivity: planning, milestones, reviews
  • Collaborate with Product teams to:
    • Reshape and grow our platform capabilities to enable product teams 
    • Define and deliver industry leading, open-source, zero-touch APM instrumentation
  • Stay technically close to the work — apply strong technical judgment, set a high standard for quality, contribute code where it matters most, and keep quality and architecture high
  • Build strong relationships and drive alignment across the language teams and product, backend
  • Shape team identity and culture

Who you are

  • An experienced Engineering Manager with a track record of shipping 
  • A strong and empathetic leader with the ability to build and lead high-performing teams to deliver high quality software
  • An ability pivot from high level product narratives to highly technical implementation details 
  • You have significant programming experience in one or more of: Go, C, Rust
  • Bonus: If you possess experience with one or more of these skills: systems programming experience, observability tooling experience, experience shipping client side software, Go runtime expertise

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. 

Benefits and Growth

  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
  • Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing
  • Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking
  • An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)
  • Access to Inclusion Talks, our Internal panel discussions
  • Free, global mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+
  • Competitive global benefits


Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. title: Administrative Business Partner, GTM - London
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-starting Administrative Business Partner to support senior Go-To-Market leaders at Anthropic. This role requires exceptional administrative efficiency and flawless execution to manage leaders' scheduling, logistics, and communications. You will maintain immaculate systems to ensure no details slip through the cracks while providing comprehensive support. As a critical point of contact, you will need to demonstrate exceptional organizational abilities in a fast-paced, high-volume environment, maintaining meticulous systems while handling shifting priorities. Success requires outstanding attention to detail, strong relationship-building skills, and the ability to anticipate needs across teams while ensuring responsive, error-free execution.

Responsibilities:

  • Scheduling and managing calendars for leader(s) and their organization(s), supporting with tracking and execution of action items

  • Building and maintaining organizational systems for tracking and managing inbound requests

  • Managing the leader's inbox and communications with precise attention to detail, maintaining rapid response times and ensuring all messages are swiftly triaged

  • Providing seamless and welcoming experiences for in-person visitors, ensuring prospective external partners feel valued and appreciated

  • Handling travel logistics and coordinating logistics for conferences and events in partnership with comms, sales, and marketing teams. 

  • Coordinating with internal stakeholders to gather necessary information and materials for meetings

  • Managing expense claims and reimbursements for leaders, ensuring timely processing and accurate record-keeping

  • Assisting with ad-hoc projects using your problem-solving skills and proactive mindset to drive positive outcomes

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Are highly organized with the ability to build systems to track and prioritize multiple tasks

  • Maintain a high level of attention to detail in fast-paced and changing environments and take pride in flawless administrative execution

  • Have experience working in heavily external facing Executive support roles

  • Have enthusiasm for supporting leaders in executing their vision, and ensuring they have the necessary resources and information to succeed

  • Have excellent time management skills

  • Have a positive, calm, and welcoming attitude and are able to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels

  • Have a proven track record of handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion

Strong candidates may also have:

  • A strong interest in Anthropic’s mission and deep commitment to AI safety in research and product development

  • Experience supporting executives or busy leaders

  • A security mindset with a thorough understanding of data protection and privacy best practices

Role-Specific Location Policy: 

  • Currently, we expect all staff to be in our office at least 25% of the time. For this role specifically, however, we expect it may be necessary to be in the office more regularly, around 3-4 days a week.

 

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
£145,000—£145,000 GBP

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Mid-Market Customer Success Manager - Americas
description: About this Role Hi, I’m Denise , and I’m the Head of High-Touch (Mid-Market) Customer Success at Ashby. Our team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional customer experience for our high-touch customer segment, which primarily supports mid-market and growth-stage organizations. I’m excited to be hiring our next CSM as we continue expanding globally. As a member of our Customer Success team, you will help us continue to grow our High-Touch Customer Success function. In this role, you’ll partner closely with customers to drive adoption, deliver strategic guidance, conduct product trainings and partnership reviews, and identify opportunities for expanded use cases and long-term value realization. You’ll also collaborate with a talented group of CSMs across the High-Touch team to continuously evolve how we support companies ranging from high-growth startups to public enterprises. Ashby is designed to be powerful and flexible, allowing customers to tailor the platform to their unique hiring processes and workflows. Because of this, there is a lot to learn. You will become both a product and domain expert, enabling customers to make the most of Ashby and drive hiring excellence across their organizations. Role Requirements: You have a strong track record of Customer Success experience in B2B SaaS (at least two years), supporting customers through the adoption and long-term optimization of complex technologies. You enjoy building trusted partnerships with customers and helping them realize measurable value throughout the customer lifecycle. You have experience managing a portfolio of approximately 60 mid-market customers with over $1.5M in total ARR. You’re comfortable balancing proactive engagement across a broad book of business while building strong relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders to drive adoption, retention, and growth. You have experience partnering cross-functionally with teams such as Sales, Marketing, Product, Support, and Operations to advocate for customer needs and deliver a seamless customer experience. You enjoy becoming a product expert and have demonstrated this in previous Customer Success roles. You create “aha” moments by tailoring trainings, workflow guidance, and strategic recommendations to each customer’s unique goals and challenges. You’ve worked with technically complex products and bring strong curiosity and problem-solving skills to understanding how systems, workflows, and integrations operate in practice You Should Apply If: 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms. 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as providing the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our product roadmap continues delivering value. 📊You enjoy working with a larger book of varied customers, and can effectively prioritise your time to make the biggest impact. 🧩 You’re energized by learning and supporting a complex product. You enjoy diving deep into technical details, navigating advanced configurations, and data workflows, and you enjoy helping customers make sense of them. 🧑‍🏫 You love to teach. Whether it’s a complex report to a very tenured data analyst, or a workflow to a brand new recruiter, who is new to SaaS tools, you see every teaching moment as an opportunity. 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You obsess over sending crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates. ⚡️ You move fast. You leverage tools/technology to maximize your time. You are at home managing a wide range of customers, and prioritizing effectively. 🗺️ You're energized by an ever-improving work environment. Our team is growing, and continually iterating on processes - we live by our Operating Principle of "Implement Continuous Improvement" 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data. Why you shouldn’t apply: You thrive with a smaller, more focused book of customers,. Our Mid-Market CSMs typically manage a book of 60+ customers, balancing personalized relationships with efficient, scalable support. You're interested in managing customer accounts with well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work) You shine as an exclusively commercial CSM, motivated by variable compensation. While our team's north star metric is revenue retention, we focus on adoption and engagement as our leading indicators. For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a lovely team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay. You’re afraid of rolling up your sleeves. If the idea of getting in the weeds with a customer about the nuance between a time in process report and a time to hire report feels too granular, or project managing a workflow change for offer approvals feels “beneath you”, this job isn’t going to be for you. About Ashby We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website: https://www.ashbyhq.com/ We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀 Interview Process Our interview process is thorough - we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows: Intro Call with Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes Hiring Manager Interview - 45 Minutes Mock Customer Call - 45 Minutes Final Round - 1 hour Rather than a traditional panel interview with a large group, we structure our panel into two focused conversations. This gives you the opportunity to meet with multiple team members in a more conversational setting centered on specific topics, instead of a formal Q&A. You'll discuss how you approach problem solving, dive into a product complexity exercise, then wrap up with a quick closing call with the hiring manager. Benefits You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks is recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅 Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US . We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. title: Sr. Support Operations Manager
description: Hello! I'm Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Support at Ashby is a strategic differentiator. As we've scaled, we've built out dedicated functions to support it: a Systems Engineer keeping our tooling running, a Workforce Management practice ensuring we have the right coverage at the right times, a Quality program that keeps every interaction excellent, and a Training function that gets new hires up to speed fast. Each of these functions is strong on its own. What we're missing is someone to bring them together. That's why we're hiring our first Senior Support Operations Manager to lead the Support Operations organization: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training. You'll report directly to me. This role isn't about running any one of these functions day to day. It's about setting the systems, processes, and standards that let them work together, coaching and developing the leaders who own them, and ensuring the systems and processes behind Support match the customer experience we want to deliver. You won't own the hands-on systems administration, forecasting, quality evaluations, or training delivery, but you'll be expected to understand that work well enough to ask sharp questions, spot patterns across functions, and have real problem-solving conversations with the leads who own it day to day. You'll also be a key partner to our Knowledge Management team, helping turn what we know into self-service and in-app experiences that reduce the need for a ticket in the first place. If you love building operational rigor while creating an environment where team members are eager to grow, staying close enough to the work to coach from firsthand understanding, and treating efficiency and quality as two sides of the same coin, this might be the role for you. Our team will be at our company offsite from October 5-9. Applications will remain open during that time, and we’ll begin reviewing them the week of October 12. About the role As the Senior Support Operations Manager, you'll own the strategy, standards, and coordination across Ashby's Support Operations functions. You'll manage through the leaders who own each function's day-to-day execution, but you'll stay close to the work by regularly reviewing QA scores, joining forecasting reviews, and understanding systems changes well enough that your coaching is specific, not just directional. Because this is a new layer of leadership and Support Operations is still being established, you'll have the authority to define how these functions coordinate, where they should be more tightly integrated, and where efficiency gains can free up capacity for higher-impact work. In your first year, you'll establish consistent processes and standards across the four functions, formalize how the functions work together, and help drive measurable improvements in efficiency or quality. What you’ll own: Integrating Systems, WFM, Quality, and Training Manage and coordinate Support Operations' four functions: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, ensuring they operate as a cohesive organization supporting our Specialists and Support Engineers. Plan and implement operational policies, standards, and recurring practices that bring consistency across functions while respecting what makes each one distinct. Identify where functions should work more closely together (e.g., how Quality findings inform Training content, or how WFM forecasts should account for Systems changes) and drive that integration. Managing and Developing the Leaders of Each Function Directly manage the leaders and individual contributors across Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, including several who are new to their roles and still establishing their own operating standards. Coach and develop the leaders of each function as they grow their programs, hire their teams, and establish operating standards, grounding that coaching in specific, detailed feedback. Driving Performance and Efficiency Across Functions Stay close to each function's day-to-day workflows, metrics, and constraints so you can spot patterns and ensure excellence in delivery. Evaluate operational performance and efficiency across all four functions, using data to identify where the organization is succeeding and where opportunity remains. Champion efficiency gains as a core goal alongside quality, not in tension with it. Build the visibility leaders need to understand tradeoffs across systems reliability, coverage, quality, and training investment. Representing Support Operations Cross-Functionally Act as a thought partner to Support Leadership on how strong systems and processes help Support be a strategic differentiator for Ashby. Represent Support Operations in cross-functional conversations with Engineering, Product, and People Ops. Help redefine what an exceptional customer experience looks like as the underlying team and tooling continue to scale. What This Role Requires: Operational Leadership Experience Proven experience leading operational functions in a Support or Customer Experience organization, with depth in one or more disciplines and experience coordinating across multiple disciplines (e.g., systems, workforce management, quality, or training). Experience managing managers or leaders of distinct functions, hiring and developing teams, and building clear ownership across multiple functions. You stay close enough to the work to inspect quality, challenge assumptions, and coach effectively, without needing to be the primary operator for each function. Track record of building or scaling operational standards and processes across a growing organization. Systems Thinking and Cross-Functional Coordination Strong ability to see how distinct functions interact and to design clear ways for them to work together. You use operational data to identify problems, make tradeoffs, and hold teams accountable to measurable outcomes. Comfort working in ambiguity, especially where functions are new and their processes and standards are still being defined. Coaching Leaders and Specialists Skilled at coaching leaders and specialists at different stages of maturity, from those establishing a new function to those refining an existing one. Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to align stakeholders across Systems, WFM, Quality, Training, Knowledge Management, and Support Leadership, tailoring context for different audiences. Genuine investment in developing people, beyond managing outputs. Strategic Thinking and Customer Focus Believes Support is a strategic differentiator, not a cost center, and can articulate why. Passionate about efficiency and quality as complementary goals rather than competing priorities. Excited about self-service and in-app support as levers for a better customer experience, not just cost reduction. You should apply if: You enjoy leading through managers and functional leaders, developing them through specific feedback while staying close enough to the work to coach effectively. You're energized by helping establish an operating model from the ground up, bringing structure, clear ownership, and coordination to distinct disciplines that are still being built. You use data to make tradeoffs, hold teams accountable to outcomes, and prove that efficiency and quality can reinforce each other. You're excited to help build the organization through active hiring and cross-functional partnership, and to shape how customers experience Ashby. You should not apply if: You want to be the primary operator or subject-matter expert in one function rather than lead through managers across several. You need fully mature, fully staffed functions and established processes and standards to step into. You're uncomfortable using data to make tradeoffs, setting standards where none exist, or operating in ambiguity. You see efficiency and quality as inherently in tension rather than as goals to pursue together. About Ashby Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com . About Go To Market We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell. We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. title: AI Outbound Marketing Manager
description: Hi, I’m Tim ! I run Scaled Outbound at Ashby. We’ve spent the last year building the system: campaign architecture, the tooling stack, and the automated email and LinkedIn motion that reaches buyers with thoughtful messaging at a volume no human team can match. Here’s where it breaks. The moment a campaign ships, my attention is already pulled to the next priority. So the work that makes a good campaign great isn’t happening with the level of care it deserves; refreshing and optimizing copy before it fatigues, finding creative new hooks by pulling in from the amazing content library and listening infrastructure, and partnering with other members of the team to create a complete ‘happy prospect > customer journey’. This role exists to close this gap. We’re looking for someone who is deeply curious, with great taste, and who gets energy from optimizing campaigns to perfection, institutionalizing learnings, and scaling the learnings we have from across the business into the most thoughtful, genuinely valuable, and high-converting campaigns. You can think of yourself as the owner of everything that happens after a Scaled Outbound campaign goes live. What you’ll be responsible for in this role Optimizing and scaling outbound campaigns. You will develop highly iterative experimentation methodology sprints to constantly improve the quality of existing campaigns and ensure we land the right message, at the right time, with the right contact. Keep the automated motion from going stale. You’ll co-own the email and LinkedIn sequences with the Program Manager. Sequence refresh, new angles, and killing fatigue before it shows up in the numbers. A big part of success in this role is ensuring automated motion gets better over time instead of aging out. Own copy optimization and conversion. You’re copy-obsessed. You can look at an underperforming sequence, understand why, and then fix it. This includes owning the Twain prompt library that shapes our 1:1 generated copy, tuning it so personalization at volume reads like a sharp human wrote it, not a machine. Turn performance data into action. You’ll own QA and performance analysis for the automated motion and be able to quickly and decisively conclude what is and isn’t working, and then have the curiosity and first principle thinking to know how to redesign and optimize your way into conversion. Collate and integrate materials and learnings from Sales, PMM, and Content. You’ll work directly with Sales Managers, Product Marketing, and Content to pull fresh proof points, launches, and data into active sequences, so the messaging always reflects our sharpest current story. Co-own program-level physical touches. The programs will vary from ICP-tailored gifting (never airpods) to event invitations, and user group meetups. The stack you’ll work in: Clay, Hubspot, Instantly, HeyReach, and Twain. You don’t need to have used all of these before, but you should be the kind of person who gets fluent in a new tool quickly. You’ll Probably Love This Role If You have a creative experimental mindset, strong opinions about what good copy looks like, and no fear of testing unconventional approaches You’re energized by optimization, not just creation. You’d rather make a live campaign convert 20% better than write a brand-new one from scratch You’re copy and customer obsessed, you take time to understand the buyer and can diagnose why a sequence is underperforming, then act on it You read campaign performance data fluently and turn it into the next play You’ve run cold outbound sequences before (email or LinkedIn) You like owning something horizontal that raises the performance of every campaign the team builds The background we’re looking for There are two paths into this role and we’re open to both: Marketing side. Demand gen, growth, or lifecycle/outbound marketing at a B2B SaaS company, where you personally wrote and optimized cold sequences rather than briefing them. Sales side. You've spent multiple years in outbound sales, starting as a BDR/SDR. If you moved into an AE role, you kept running your own outbound. You built your own lists, wrote your own sequences, and sourced a meaningful share of your pipeline from cold outbound at real volume. Either way, what we’re actually looking for is the same: You’ve written cold email and/or LinkedIn sequences and been measured on what they produced You’ve worked in a sequencing or sales engagement tool (Instantly, Smartlead, HeyReach, or similar) and can read performance data without waiting on an analyst/ops You reach for AI to compress your own work, whether that’s research, first drafts, pattern-finding in performance data, or building something small to save yourself time You care about pipeline, not MQLs This role is not for you if You want to primarily write long-form or brand content. You think a live campaign on auto-enroll is done You prefer a locked playbook. A lot of this is defining what “great” looks like from first principles You’re uncomfortable being measured on the performance of a system you didn’t build from the ground up You get overwhelmed by the detailed work of optimizing (sequence refresh, localization, reporting, QA, swapping content) You’d rather own a single campaign end-to-end than raise the floor on all of them Your outbound experience is agency-side or brand-side rather than in-house at a B2B SaaS company You've briefed copy but haven't personally written and shipped cold sequences You need an analyst to tell you what the campaign data says Interview Plan Our interview process is: 30 minutes intro call with Michelle (Recruiter Screen) 45 minutes interview with Tim McCann (Hiring Manager) 30 minutes interview with Harriet (VP Marketing) 30 min take home review Tim, Harriet, Sam Final panel: 30 minutes with Claire (Demand Gen) 30 minutes with Sam (SMB Sales Leader) 30 minutes with Lia (Product Marketing Leader) Benefits Competitive salary and equity. Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team. 10-year exercise window for stock options . You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅. Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us and a 401k match. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. title: Integrations Lead, Partnerships - AMER
description: Hi 👋, I’m Kat :) when I joined Ashby two and a half years ago to lead Partnerships, we had less than a hundred integrations. Today, we have over 300 , thanks to exceptional work from Hannah to take us from 0 to 1, our Product Managers, and our Engineers. As our integration ecosystem continues to grow, we’re looking for someone to take on Integrations as a full scope, including building out our integration ecosystem for new products (like People Workflows). As the Integrations Lead, Partnerships , you’ll report directly to me and be responsible for owning our integration partnerships across inbound, outbound and account management, and being the technical liaison for our Product Managers and Engineering team. This is a highly cross-functional role that requires strong communication and collaboration with Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, Product, and Marketing. You’ll have the opportunity to be on the front lines of trending HR Tech by speaking to inbound partners and guiding them on the best practices for developing their use case against our APIs . Success in this role looks like maintaining a strong sense of ownership over the partner experience and prioritizing how we can be helpful, while being direct and clear about our customer-first mindset. You’ll take over account management for our larger partners, like ADP, and find ways to continue improving how companies integrate with Ashby. What you’ll do Own the inbound integration lifecycle Own inbound integration requests from qualification through launch and ongoing maintenance, using judgment about customer value, product fit, technical feasibility, partner commitment, and Ashby’s priorities. Guide partners through the process—from NDA and sandbox access to API documentation, onboarding, testing, and launch—while choosing the right balance of async and live collaboration. Set clear expectations, keep work moving, and close the loop thoughtfully when an integration is not the right fit or a current priority. Connect partners, Product, and Engineering Serve as the technical and commercial liaison across integration partners and Ashby’s Product, Engineering, Product Operations, Support, Customer Success, Sales, and Marketing teams. Translate partner and customer needs into clear requirements, tradeoffs, and next steps, and help determine the right path: native build, partner-built integration, connector, unified API, or future roadmap opportunity. Help partners navigate API concepts such as authentication, endpoints, webhooks, data mapping, and workflow design, while bringing sound judgment to design-partner and enterprise requests. Own how integration knowledge reaches Sales, CS,and Support, so teams feel well versed on current and upcoming integrations. Own quality, launches, and strategic partnerships Coordinate integration reviews and launch readiness with partners and Product, including workflow validation, feedback, security considerations, configuration, documentation, assets, and Marketplace publication. Maintain the external integration directory and partner-facing resources, and partner with Marketing and Product Marketing on launch communications, enablement, and ongoing updates. Manage larger integration relationships, working with Enterprise Sales, Customer Success, and Product to understand customer needs, enterprise opportunities, design-partner requirements, and roadmap implications. Represent Ashby externally in partner discovery, technical scoping, roadmap conversations, launches, and post-launch feedback loops. Optimize current integrations when updates arise, coordinating scope with Project Managers and aligning with partners and internally. Improve the operational foundations for scale Keep HubSpot and related partnership systems current with partner context, status, ownership, timelines, and customer or prospect demand. Improve swim lanes, handoffs, SLAs, documentation, reporting, and support paths as you operate the program. Automate high-frequency, low-variance work while preserving human judgment for qualification, prioritization, quality review, and strategic relationship management. Work directly with the knowledge base team to build out systems for keeping integration documentation up-to-date. About You We think the ideal person for this role will have experience and skills that look something like this: You’ve worked at the intersection of partnerships, product, technology, and customers—in integration or platform partnerships, technical program management, product management, solutions architecture, implementation, or a similar role. You’re technically fluent enough to understand APIs, authentication, data flows, webhooks, sandboxes, and integration tradeoffs. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable asking precise questions and learning how systems work. You bring strong product and business judgment: you can distinguish between an interesting request, a customer problem, a strategic opportunity, and a commitment Ashby should make. You communicate clearly and write well. You can build trust with partners, set expectations, give direct guidance, and turn messy conversations into crisp requirements, decisions, and documentation. You’re operationally disciplined and improvement-minded. You can own a high-volume workstream, create structure in ambiguity, automate repetitive work, and follow through across teams. You care deeply about the customer experience and can work effectively across Product, Engineering, Support, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and external partners. You like building the system, not just running it. You're drawn to finding a problem, scoping it, and proposing a solution, and you don't assume the current way is the right way just because it's what exists. This role probably isn’t right if… You want a role focused only on strategy or relationship development; this role includes hands-on technical, operational, and documentation work. You’re uncomfortable with technical detail, difficult prioritization decisions, or direct conversations about fit and expectations. You prefer an established playbook or a single-function role rather than building structure across teams. You dislike writing, async communication, proactive follow-up, or representing Ashby externally. You are unable to work across time zones or travel occasionally for partner and team moments. You get overwhelmed by your inbox. This role requires timely follow up and holding a high bar for timely communication. You dislike being on calls or you’re uncomfortable leading a meeting that includes customer leads, partner leads, and Ashby Product Managers. No pressure to buy your options until it financially makes sense for you. Unlimited PTO with a strong culture of actually taking time off. 12 weeks of fully paid family leave (US). Generous budget for equipment, software, and office setup. $100/month learning budget, with conferences covered with manager approval. Top-tier health insurance for US employees (100% premium covered). We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. title: Principal, Analyst Relations Lead
description: Hi 👋I’m Kat and I lead Partnerships at Ashby. I joined Ashby in April 2024 to build the Partnerships function from zero. The through-line in my career has been to build in spaces where no precedent existed. Which is similar to how Harriet is building the broader Marketing function at Ashby: using first principles to think about what we really need to get to our desired results. Over the past ~2 years, our business has grown to be the default operating system for over 5,000 of the most ambitious companies in tech, finance, and healthcare. Our Partnerships team has also grown from just me, to a team of 5 located across the US and Europe. We currently look after a variety of programs that are central to our growth: VC Partnerships, Ashby Experts, Integrations, Community Activation, and more. As a team, we’re focused on delivering outsized value to our partners, customers, and broader TA community – and delivering moments of unreasonable hospitality along the way. As we continue to grow and solidify our position upmarket, I’m looking for someone to lead Analyst Relations globally. You’ll have fantastic partners in PMM, as well as buy in from our Executive Leadership Team to make sure we’re delivering and refining our product narrative to the right firms, at the right time. This isn’t a traditional AR role. The right person for this role will feel at ease becoming a product expert in addition to building strong relationships that convert to qualified pipeline, and have a sharp instinct for when to engage and when an opportunity isn’t for us. If this sounds appealing, we’d love to hear from you!
